name: Draft Angle Checker
blurb: minimum draft angle for release from a mould
intro: The least draft a wall needs to leave the tool, and what that draft does to the wall over its depth. Injection moulding uses the SPI-finish and Mold-Tech texture rules, die casting the NADCA draft formula; the other processes use common rules of thumb.

inputs.label: Texture depth
inputs.help: From the texture chart, e.g. MT-11010 about 25 µm (0.001 in).

inputs.label: Your draft (to check)
inputs.help: Leave empty to see only the recommendation.

examples.title: Textured ABS housing wall, 30 mm deep
Aluminium die-cast rib, inside wall 15 mm deep

usage: Give the process, the finish (injection) or alloy and wall type (die casting), the wall depth in mm along the pull direction and optionally the draft you drew in degrees. It returns the minimum and recommended draft per side in degrees, the wall offset in mm over the depth, and flags a drawn draft that is too small. Use it when adding draft to a moulded or cast CAD part.
sources: NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings, section 4A: draft D = √L / C
Mold-Tech / Standex texture guideline: 1.5° per 0.001 in of texture depth
Protolabs injection moulding design guide: draft by SPI finish, 1° per inch of depth
Sand, investment, silicone, vacuum forming and rubber drafts: rule of thumb
